name: Shaphat
title: The Spy from the Tribe of Simeon
summary: Shaphat, son of Hori, was the representative from the tribe of Simeon among the twelve spies that Moses sent to explore the land of Canaan. He is best known for his role in the spying mission described in Numbers. The name Shaphat means 'he has judged' and also appears as the name of several other biblical figures, including the father of the prophet Elisha.

keyEvents.title: Selected as a Scout
keyEvents.description: Shaphat was chosen by Moses to represent the tribe of Simeon in scouting the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: The Scouting Mission to Canaan
keyEvents.description: Shaphat was among the twelve scouts sent from the wilderness of Paran to explore the land of Canaan and report back on the land and its people.

keyEvents.title: Exploring the Land
keyEvents.description: The scouts, including Shaphat, traveled through Canaan from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob and explored the land for forty days.

keyEvents.title: Negative Majority Report
keyEvents.description: Upon their return, the majority of the scouts, likely including Shaphat, gave a negative report that the land could not be conquered, even though it flowed with milk and honey. Only Joshua and Caleb spoke against this view.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on the Scouts
keyEvents.description: Because of the negative report and lack of faith, the ten scouts who spread fear among the people, including Shaphat, were struck by a plague and died in the Lord's presence.
